title: Injuries resulting from falls of standing trucks
summary:
When working on stationary commercial vehicles, employees work at heights of two to four meters. Falls sometimes result in serious injuries and often occur when exiting the cab, as well as during loading and unloading. One risk factor is likely falling backward, as the impact cannot be reduced by streching the arms.
To date, reports have primarily focused on the frequency of truck fall accidents and accident mechanisms. For this reason, this study aims to analyze clinical data focusing on the consequences of injuries and potential medical risk factors for severe injuries in truck fall accidents. The results are intended to help incorporate the medical aspects of fall accidents into the design of preventive measures.
conditions: Acute traumatic injuries resulting from a truck rollover accident

interventions.name: A retrospective cohort study analyzing routine data from patients who presented to the emergency department of Unfallkrankenhaus Berlin between January 1, 2016, and December 31, 2025, following a fall from a standing truck.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Falling from a truck as a driver, passenger, or helper during loading or unloading
Exclusion criteria:
Patient has been treated outside the defined inclusion period
